evidence.quote: For Robie was the logical conclusion of the development of vending machines. All the earlier ones had stood in one place, on a floor or hanging on a wall, and blankly delivered merchandise in return for coins, whereas Robie searched for customers.
evidence.paraphrase: Robie is presented as a mobile sales robot that actively seeks out customers, an advance over stationary vending machines.

evidence.quote: The lower part of Robie's body was a metal hemisphere hemmed with sponge rubber and not quite touching the sidewalk. The upper was a metal box with black holes in it. The box could swivel and duck.
evidence.paraphrase: Robie's physical construction and mechanism are described in technical detail.

evidence.quote: Robie radared the crowd, found that it surrounded him solidly, and stopped.
evidence.paraphrase: Robie uses radar-based sensing to detect the crowd around him.

evidence.quote: At this age-level, Robie's reference silhouettes permitted him to distinguish sex, though with occasional amusing and embarrassing miscalls.
evidence.paraphrase: Robie identifies people using stored reference silhouettes, with limits to the recognition system.

evidence.quote: The silver-green was a newly developed paint that foiled radar.
evidence.paraphrase: The incoming projectile uses a newly developed radar-defeating paint.

evidence.quote: Just three seconds later, the silver-green bud bloomed above Manhattan into a globular orange flower. The skyscrapers grew brighter and brighter still, the brightness of the inside of the Sun. The windows winked blossoming white fire-flowers.
evidence.paraphrase: A nuclear-style explosion detonates over Manhattan.

evidence.quote: The crowd around Robie bloomed, too. Their clothes puffed into petals of flame. Their heads of hair were torches.
evidence.paraphrase: The blast incinerates the surrounding crowd.

evidence.quote: It was wonderful to be alive and watching Robie on such an exciting day.
evidence.paraphrase: The oblivious contentment of the crowd is stated just before the impending disaster known to the reader.

evidence.quote: (But way, way up, where the crowd could not see, the sky was darker still. Purple-dark, with stars showing. And in that purple-dark, a silver-green something, the color of a bud, plunged down at better than three miles a second.
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator informs the reader of an approaching threat that the crowd cannot see.

evidence.quote: But the customer had run away, screaming, and Robie never ran after customers
evidence.paraphrase: A burned survivor flees in terror while Robie continues its sales routine.

evidence.quote: "Hello, youngster," Robie said. Then, after a long pause, "Cat got your tongue? Well, I have a little present for you. A nice, lovely polly-lop.
evidence.paraphrase: Robie addresses a fire hydrant as a child, obliviously continuing its sales script amid the disaster.

evidence.quote: The little girl began to cry.
evidence.paraphrase: A surviving child cries while pleading with Robie for help.

evidence.quote: "Stay right here," Robie said reassuringly, "and don't be frightened. I will call a policeman." He whistled shrilly, twice.
evidence.paraphrase: Robie offers routine reassurance and calls for police who will not come amid the devastation.

evidence.quote: But Robie had gone off to peddle Poppy Pop to the members of a rescue squad which had just come around the corner, more robotlike in their asbestos suits than he in his metal skin.
evidence.paraphrase: The story closes with Robie mechanically continuing to sell products to a rescue squad.

evidence.quote: Those who were usually bought anywhere from one to five hundred shares, if they had any money and foresight enough to see that sales robots would eventually be on every street and highway in the country.
evidence.paraphrase: It is projected that sales robots will proliferate across the nation.

evidence.quote: Alive and amused in the fresh, weather-controlled air between the lines of bright skyscrapers with their winking windows and under a sky so blue you could almost call it dark.
